/**
 * Provides static methods for generating keyboard template blocks from `LabelKeyboard` definitions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This class generates HTML-like `<keyboard>` blocks for the template engine. Requires `LabelKeyboard` to be set via {@link BlockKeyboard.label} before using {@link BlockKeyboard._build}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // blocks/keyboard.ts
 * import { BlockKeyboard, LabelKeyboard } from "gramstax";
 *
 * class KeyboardBlock extends BlockKeyboard {
 *   static label = class extends LabelKeyboard {
 *     static backNext = {en: "Back, Next", id: "Kembali, Lanjut"}
 *   }
 *   static backNext = (lang?: string, type?: string) => this._build(`backNext`, lang, type)
 * }
 *
 * // base/page.ts
 * import {KeyboardBlock} from "~/blocks/keyboard"
 * export abstract class PageBase extends CtxCore {
 *   static kbk = KeyboardBlock
 *   static kbl = KeyboardBlock.label
 * }
 *
 * // pages/some.ts
 * import {PageBase} from "~/base/page"
 * export class SomePage extends PageBase {
 *   static template = `
 *     <base>
 *       ${this.kbk.backNext()}
 *       <message>Default message hello world</message>
 *     </base>
 *     <base id="others-id-1">
 *       <message>Message from others id 1 with keyboard from base id default</message>
 *     </base>
 *     <base id="others-id-2">
 *       <base>${this.kbk.backNext()}</base>
 *       <message>Message from others id 3 with keyboard in same base</message>

/**
 * Extends {@link https://github.com/jaredwray/keyv | Keyv} to provide a unified caching interface with built-in support for memory and Redis storage.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Storage modes: - **Memory mode:** when `url` is `"memory"` (default), uses an in-memory `Map`. - **Redis mode:** when `url` starts with `"redis"`, uses `@keyv/redis` adapter. - **Custom mode:** when `more.forceStore` is provided, uses the custom store.
 *
 * @typeParam V - The type of values stored in the cache.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { CacheExternal } from "gramstax";
 *
 * // Memory cache (default)
 * const memoryCache = new CacheExternal();
 *
 * // Redis cache
 * const redisCache = new CacheExternal("redis://localhost:6379", 3600000, "s");
 *
 * // With namespace and TTL
 * const cache = new CacheExternal("memory", 60000, "myapp");
 *
 * // Set and get data
 * await cache.set("user:123", { name: "John" });
 * const user = await cache.get("user:123");
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: CacheExternal

 * import {Menu2Page} from "./menu2"

 *   async callback() {
 *     const kb = this.inlineKeyboardT([Menu1Page, Menu2Page])

/**
 * Static utility class for parsing and compiling HTML-like templates.

 * @remarks
 *
 * The `TemplateEngine` provides methods for parsing HTML-like template syntax with custom blocks (base, message, keyboard, media, description, etc.) and compiling them into executable functions. It supports variable interpolation, conditional rendering, array mapping, script execution, and template imports.

 * Templates are typically organized into `<base>` blocks containing various content blocks like `<message>`, `<keyboard>`, `<media>`, and `<description>`. Each block supports a `lang` attribute for internationalization.

 *     <keyboard>Back, Next</keyboard>
 *     <message>Welcome {{name}}!</message>
 *   </base>
 * `;
 *
 * const messages = TemplateEngine.compileMessages(template);
 * const keyboards = TemplateEngine.compileKeyboards(template);
 *
 * const msg = messages.default.default({ name: 'John' });
 * // Result: 'Welcome John!'
 * ```

/**
 * Compiles keyboard blocks from a template into executable functions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method parses `<keyboard>` blocks from the template and compiles them into functions that generate button label arrays. The result is organized by base ID and language, with separate `inline` and `bottom` keyboard modes. Comma-separated labels are split into individual button strings.
 *
 * @param template - Raw template string containing `<base>` and `<keyboard>` blocks
 *
 * @param baseBlocks - Optional pre-parsed base blocks for reuse
 *
 * @returns Compiled keyboard functions organized by base ID, language, and mode
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <base>
 *     <keyboard>Yes, No, {{action}}</keyboard>
 *     <keyboard type="bottom">Menu, Help</keyboard>
 *   </base>
 * `;
 * const keyboards = TemplateEngine.compileKeyboards(template);
 * const inline = keyboards.default.default.inline?.({ action: 'Cancel' });
 * // Result: ['Yes', 'No', 'Cancel']
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: compileKeyboards

/**
 * Recursively processes and resolves `<import>` blocks in a template.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method resolves all `<import>` directives in a template by calling the provided resolver function to fetch external template content. It supports recursive imports with a depth limit of 10 to prevent infinite loops. An optional cache can be provided to avoid redundant resolutions.
 *
 * @param template - Template string containing `<import>` directives
 *
 * @param resolver - Function that resolves import sources to template content
 *
 * @param depth - Current recursion depth (defaults to 0)
 *
 * @param importCache - Optional Map to cache resolved imports for reuse
 *
 * @returns Template with all `<import>` blocks resolved and replaced
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = '<import src="header" block="message" />\n<message>Main content</message>';
 * const resolver = (src: string) => {
 *   if (src === 'header') return '<message>Header text</message>';
 *   return null;
 * };
 * const result = TemplateEngine.processImportBlocks(template, resolver);
 * // Result: '<message>Header text</message>\n<message>Main content</message>'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: processImportBlocks

/**
 * Manages template loading, compilation, caching, and hot-reloading from page files.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The `TemplateManager` class provides a centralized system for handling templates used in Gramstax bots. It supports: - Loading templates from static `template` properties in page classes - Loading templates from external `.html` files - Hot-reloading templates during development via file watching - Multi-language support with fallback to `default`
 *
 * Templates are compiled once and cached for efficient retrieval.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import {TemplateManager} from "gramstax"
 * import {join} from "path"
 *
 * const tm = new TemplateManager({
 *   path: [join(process.cwd(), "src", "pages")],
 *   enableWatch: process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"
 * })
 *
 * // Get a compiled message
 * const message = tm.getMessage("start", "default", "en", {name: "John"})
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Initialize a worker thread export with automatic environment detection.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * In worker thread context, only returns `launchGatewayClient`. In main thread context, returns full proxy with `launchWorker`, `launchGatewayClient`, and all worker methods.
 *

 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // jobs/counter.ts
 * import { WorkerThreadExport, WorkerThreadInit } from "gramstax";
 *

 *
 *   mtdGetCount() {
 *     return this.count;
 *   }
 * }
 *
 * export const CounterJob = WorkerThreadExport.init({
 *   path: __filename,
 *   WTInit: Worker,
 * });
 *
 * // main.ts
 * import { CounterJob } from "./jobs/counter";
 *
 * await CounterJob.launchWorker();
